content:
RESOLVED that the planning application
be REFUSED permission for the following reasons:

·       
The proposed development fails to safeguard the countryside from
encroachment, thereby by undermining the remaining Green Belt, and
is in an unsustainable location with poor access to public
transport and local facilities and services. It is therefore
considered contrary to Policy CS01 Sustainable Development, Policy
CS02 Scale and Distribution of Development of the Local Plan Core
Strategy (2014), and the requirements of Para. 155 of the National
Planning Policy Framework (2024).

·       
The proposed development would be inappropriate by definition. It
would cause substantial harm to the Green Belt’s openness and
in the absence of very special circumstances to clearly outweigh
the potential harm to the Green Belt by reason of
inappropriateness, or any other harm resulting from the proposal.
It is therefore considered contrary to Policy CS02 Scale and
Distribution of Development of the Local Plan Core Strategy (2014),
and Section 13 Protecting Green Belt Land of the National Planning
Policy Framework 2024.

·       
The proposed development, by virtue of the increase in the number
of dwellings, would place additional demand on existing physical
and social infrastructure that is insufficient to accommodate the
scale of development proposed. The proposal would therefore give
rise to an unacceptable burden on local infrastructure, to the
detriment of both existing and future residents. For these reasons,
the development is contrary to Policy CS10 (Physical and Social
Infrastructure) of the Local Plan Core Strategy (2014).
topline: The Planning Committee has decided to refuse a planning application due to concerns about encroaching on the Green Belt and strain on local infrastructure.

the Secretary to the STG Building Control Joint Committee be
notified on approval of the Business Plan prior to the annual
meeting in June 2026; and
3.    
Cabinet noted the emerging plans for the Building Safety Levy,
which is set to go live in October 2026.
 
Note: Cllrs John Burden and
Shane Mochrie-Cox left the Chamber during consideration of this
item.
